compromise.policy: No compromise/reveal events are in scope. The attacker cannot acquire the deployment credential, forge CI metadata, modify the consumer workflow, or compromise CI infrastructure.

abstractions: GitHub Actions workflows, run records, artifact lookup responses, and deployment submissions are modeled as symbolic protocol actions rather than script semantics.
Authenticated platform statements are abstracted with auth_notify and auth_artifact terms instead of modeling concrete GitHub authentication mechanisms.
Artifact body contents are attacker-controlled or maintainer-produced opaque symbolic values; parser vulnerabilities, path traversal, cache poisoning, and arbitrary script semantics are excluded.
The three consumer configurations are isolated modes sharing the same source mechanisms.
modeling_assumptions: protected_repo and protected_branch are designated constants representing the trusted origin.
fork_repo and fork_branch are attacker-controlled origin constants distinct from the protected origin.
A branch-name string inside an artifact body is not modeled as evidence of origin.
Failed checks suppress ArtifactSelected and PrivilegedUse events for that attempted execution.
The selected body and artifact identity are taken from the same immutable artifact-store record.

semantic_constraints.policy: CIPlatform allocates fresh run IDs and records source repository, source branch, exact commit, workflow identity, completion status, and artifact for each run.
ArtifactStore creates a distinct artifact identity and records run ID, artifact name, and body; records are immutable after run completion.
Attacker can upload artifacts only as producer of fork runs and may reuse the artifact name package.
Completion notifications and artifact lookup responses are authenticated platform statements and cannot be rewritten by the attacker.
name_only selection is by artifact name package only and is not bound to the triggering run.
run_bound selection requires artifact producing_run equal to trigger_run but does not require protected repository or protected branch.
trusted_origin selection requires authenticated trigger metadata for protected_repo and protected_branch and requires exact-run artifact selection.
Selected artifacts are not relabeled as maintainer-produced merely because a privileged consumer selected them.
DeploymentService records configuration, triggering run, selected artifact, producing run, source repository, source branch, exact commit, and body.
